neighbours.label: the second digit of a two-digit chapter number in a citation of the Book of Acts ('Acts 1⟦7⟧:28'); a weaker second trigger is a crushing blow to the body (crushed, smashed, hit on the head)
fire: Lydia, a seller of purple cloth, is introduced in Acts 16:14 as the first convert in Philippi.
The sermon on the Areopagus, found in Acts 17:24, speaks of the God who made the world.
Barnabas and Saul are sent out from Antioch in Acts 13:2 after fasting and prayer.
The letter of the Jerusalem council is quoted in Acts 15:23 and the verses after it.
Paul meets Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth, as Acts 18:2 relates.
The preacher opened his Bible to Acts 14:22 and spoke about hardship.
The silversmith Demetrius stirs up the crowd in Acts 19:24 over lost trade.
Peter's defence before the other believers begins at Acts 11:4 in most editions.
quiet: The parable of the lost son is introduced in Luke 15:11 as the third in a series.
The passage on governing authorities, found in Romans 13:1, is often debated.
Peter is called the rock in Matthew 16:18 after his confession.
The saying about the way and the truth is quoted from John 14:6 and the verses after it.
Abram receives a new name in Genesis 17:5, as the story relates.
The preacher opened his Bible to Mark 13:32 and spoke about patience.
The play has 17 scenes spread over three acts and an epilogue.
The psalmist's cry for help begins at Psalm 18:6 in most editions.

notes: Probes: 'Acts 17:22' 1.17, 'Acts 19:23' 0.48, 'Acts 27:14' 0.37; 'Luke 17:21 and Romans 12:2' 0.06; '17 students' 0.01. Separately 'crushed to death' 0.58, 'hit him on the head' 0.57, 'smashed his thumb' 0.42, but 'hit the ball' 0.05. The test covers the Acts trigger only; the impact trigger is untested here, so this label is likely partial.
